fixes.explanation: Sand, baker. Moses looked this way and that, saw no one, struck down the Egyptian and hid the body in the sand (Exodus 2:12). This is a heavy moment, so I'll just say it plainly. And watch what happens next: the very next day a Hebrew asks him, "Are you planning to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?" (Exodus 2:14).

No river in this verse, friend. After looking this way and that and seeing no one, Moses hid the body in the sand (Exodus 2:12). This is a heavy moment, so I'll keep it simple. It turns out the secret didn't stay buried, because Moses thought, "This thing I have done has surely become known." (Exodus 2:14).

The text doesn't say who was losing, friend. It says Moses asked the one in the wrong, "Why are you attacking your companion?" (Exodus 2:13). That word "attacking" tells us whose behavior he was asking about. I can't even referee two people reaching for the last cookie, so I respect the nerve.

Watered, baker. Shepherds drove the daughters away, and Moses rose up to help them and watered their flock (Exodus 2:17). Think about it. He just sat down beside a well in a new land (Exodus 2:15), and a few verses later he's the one working the water. That man did not stay sitting for long.

Sheared, friend? The text says nothing about shearing here. The daughters came to draw water and fill the troughs (Exodus 2:16), and Moses watered their flock (Exodus 2:17). Water is the job on the page. I'm just a stamper, so I'll stick to what the verse says.
